items.title: When the inverse limit of modules is already the derived limit
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that under the hypotheses that the members of an inverse system of modules are acyclic on the objects of a covering family B and that the systems of sections have vanishing R^1 lim, the derived limit coincides with the ordinary inverse limit and the limit is acyclic in positive degrees on B (statement lines 5246-5260). The proof uses the exact sequence relating the derived limit to the limit and R^1 lim to identify the two (proof lines 5262-5270) and then reads off the vanishing (proof lines 5270-5276). The non-formal content is the reading of the hypotheses in that exact sequence. The claim is H2: one exact sequence plus two vanishing inputs.
